US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist. (BBC News)

pyongyang.title: North Korea supercharges crypto heists with AI skills
detail: North Korea maintains a thousands-strong hacker army, but the top unit known as "TraderTraitor" may only have a dozen or so members, experts say. (The Japan Times)

pyongyang.title: South Korea probes death of frontline soldier near North Korean border
detail: A South Korean army staff sergeant died after ‌suffering external injuries at a frontline unit in Cheorwon near the North Korean border on Monday morning, Seoul’s Defence Ministry said. Military and civilian ⁠investigators were examining the exact cause and circumstances ‌of his death, the ministry said. (South China Morning Post)

pyongyang.title: North Korea touts BBQ restaurant boom, but skeptics dismiss it as propaganda
detail: Analysts say the openings reflect a push by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un to portray a growing prosperity across the country. (The Japan Times)

pyongyang.title: Experts reportedly see North Korean links to GMO cyberattack
detail: An analysis by Japan’s GMO Internet Group found that a North Korea-linked hacking group was likely behind the cyberattack on the company last month, sources close to the matter said, citing characteristics of the malware used and other traces left by the perpetrators. (South China Morning Post)
GMO CEO Masatoshi Kumagai is set to hold the firm's first public briefing since it became embroiled in a growing scandal over a massive data breach. (The Japan Times)

pyongyang.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads: KCNA
detail: Pyongyang claimed the warhead is "capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares." (The Japan Times)
North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday, the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them. (Dawn)

singapore.title: Australia jails Singaporean tourist for fatally driving over man who stole backpack
detail: A 29-year-old Singaporean man was sentenced to five years and nine months’ jail in Australia on Monday after he killed a man who stole a backpack from his rental car. Lincoln Ng Jing Kai chased the man in a car and knocked him off his e-bike before driving over him. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Asean seeks to sign FTA with EU. Can Singapore help resolve the Myanmar hurdle?
detail: Singapore is pitching itself as a bridge between the European Union (EU) and Asean, as the two blocs continue their protracted discussions to seal a free trade agreement (FTA). (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: ‘Air-con nation’ Singapore eyes alternatives to cool down
detail: The city-state has the highest per-capita air conditioner ownership rate in Southeast Asia, with about 99% of private residences equipped with cooling units. (The Japan Times)

Long dubbed an “air-conditioned nation”, Singapore is experimenting with cooling alternatives from chilled beams to “passive displacement” to curb its thirst for energy-guzzling air conditioning. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: Do tough laws deter drug crimes? Lessons from Singapore and Malaysia
detail: As Malaysia rethinks the death penalty for drug offences, Singapore insists tough laws deter substance abuse. (Al Jazeera)

singapore.title: Will diversifying fuel imports be enough to fix Indonesia’s energy shortfall?
detail: Indonesia is looking beyond Singapore for petrol supplies as it seeks to reduce its dependence on a single source, but analysts say diversifying imports will do little to address the country’s fuel production shortfall without faster refinery modernisation and investment in alternative fuels. (South China Morning Post)

singapore.title: DPM Dar, Singaporean FM discuss ways to enhance cooperation in trade, investment
detail: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday held talks with Sin­ga­porean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, who is visiting Islamabad, and discussed ways enhance cooperation in trade and investment, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Balakrishnan arrived in Islamabad earlier in the day. (Dawn)

singapore.title: Indonesia rain set to ease toxic haze in Singapore and Malaysia
detail: The choking haze from Indonesia's worst fire season in years has cloaked local towns and drifted across neighboring countries for weeks. (The Japan Times)

singapore.title: Singapore wields ‘quiet diplomacy’ in minister’s surprise visit to Indonesia amid haze tensions
detail: Singapore’s decision to send its top diplomat to Indonesia on a surprise visit, following days of terse exchanges over a regional haze, underscores a bid to defuse growing tensions and seek a direct channel to President Prabowo Subianto. (South China Morning Post)

wellington.title: New Zealand Election: Why Cost of Living, Housing and Jobs Are Key Issues

wellington.title: Jacinda Ardern in Sydney Opera House talk advises politicians to ‘rebuild trust by building financial security’
detail: Former New Zealand prime minister has moved to Australia and is lecturing at University of Sydney – and from stage of city’s famous landmark Jacinda Ardern, who now calls Sydney home, has delivered a message to Australian politicians from the stage of the city’s Opera House. (The Guardian)

wellington.title: Former New Zealand PM Ardern to mentor students in new Australian gig
detail: SYDNEY — Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern has taken up a post at a major Australian university. Ms Ardern, who was her home country’s leader from 2017 to 2023, will soon begin guest-lecturing, running masterclasses and mentoring students and researchers at the University of Sydney. (Inquirer)

detail: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda (The Hindu)

detail: Nepal and Bhutan have jointly proposed the inclusion of a dedicated agenda item titled “1.5°C Warming in Mountains” at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, calling for stronger international action to address the escalating impacts of climate change… (Inquirer)

detail: The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, says an official (The Hindu)

detail: Ram Kumar Bhandari and his seven-member family have returned, after two months, to the same house that was buried by mud and debris in the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood. Their safety there remains uncertain. After the disaster, Bhandari rented a house in Pipaltar for about a month. (Inquirer)
